claims.text: The source specifies a subset coding problem with the empty subset excluded, but does not specify input uniqueness, value-level deduplication, output order, or size limits.
The candidate makes position-based subset semantics explicit and treats duplicate-value deduplication as a separate contract requiring clarification.
The exact Java candidate compiles and matches an independent bitmask oracle across deterministic, exhaustive, and seeded randomized cases while never emitting the empty subset.

findings: The answer stays inside the preserved non-empty-subset source boundary and labels position-based semantics as an explicit executable contract.
The exact Java implementation records only non-empty paths, advances the start index, copies mutable path state, and restores it after recursion.
Duplicate-value behavior is explicitly separated from value-level deduplication instead of silently inventing an element-uniqueness requirement.
The increasing-index-sequence argument supports both completeness and absence of position-level duplicates.
The complexity discussion includes output-copy cost rather than claiming only O(2^n).
Independent exact-candidate compilation and deterministic, exhaustive, and randomized differential validation passed.
No fabricated production experience is claimed.
